paper_title: A Survey of Chip-level Thermal Simulators

extraction.paper_title: A Survey of Chip-level Thermal Simulators

scenario.description: Survey illustration of the HotSpot flow: a floorplan plus a per-block power profile (figure labels 0.2 W, 0.2 W, 1 W, 3 W, 2 W, 2 W, 1 W) is turned into an RC circuit and solved for a per-block temperature profile (figure labels 46 C, 46.1 C, 51 C, 62 C, 57 C, 55 C, 49 C). The paper gives no block names, block coordinates or dimensions, no explicit mapping of powers to blocks, and no package or material parameters for this example. It is a schematic only, not a complete experiment, and is not a published benchmark. The packet contains no pinned assets and the paper links no code, config or data repositories.
scenario.architecture: Generic 2D chip modeled with HotSpot: a four-layer thermal RC network (die, heat spreader, heat sink, convective layer to ambient), per the text on pp. 15-16 of the survey. No chip-specific architecture is given.
scenario.workload: None specified. The figure shows an illustrative power profile only, not a benchmark or workload.
scenario.operating_point: Steady-state temperature profile for the illustrated power profile. The survey text on p. 16 states HotSpot uses a constant convection resistance of 0.8 K/W and, for its original validation, an ambient of 45 C. It does not state that these apply to the Fig. 6 example.

original_setup.solver: HotSpot: thermal RC network built from the floorplan and per-block power, solved with a 4th-order Runge-Kutta ODE solver (transient) or as a steady-state RC circuit. The four layers are die, heat spreader, heat sink and a convective layer to ambient (survey pp. 15-16, Fig. 6 on p. 16).
original_setup.optimizer: None for the Fig. 6 schematic. The survey only mentions HotSpot being used inside other works' floorplanning optimizers (simulated annealing, genetic algorithms), which are not part of this scenario (p. 16).
original_setup.controller: None. Fig. 6 shows no thermal-management controller or runtime policy.
original_setup.benchmark: None. Fig. 6 is an illustrative schematic with a floorplan, a power profile and a temperature profile. It is not a published benchmark or workload, and the packet has no pinned assets or linked repositories.

thermal_observable.location: Illustrative per-block temperature in the Fig. 6 schematic. The figure labels do not map to named blocks or coordinates, so the location is unspecified. The 62 C label is the highest value shown.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum of the seven digitized per-block steady-state labels in Fig. 6 (46, 46.1, 51, 62, 57, 55, 49 C). The paper reports no formal aggregation, so this is a figure-label reading, not a validated result.

physical_mismatches.reason: Fig. 6 is only a schematic with no named blocks, coordinates, dimensions or explicit power-to-block mapping. Block geometry and per-block power cannot be extracted, so no floorplan can be built from paper-derived facts.

No package or material parameters are given for the Fig. 6 example (die, spreader, sink thicknesses or conductivities, TIM, heat-sink dimensions). The 0.8 K/W convection resistance and 45 C ambient on p. 16 come from HotSpot's general description and original validation, and are not stated for this example.
The Fig. 6 temperatures and powers are illustrative labels with no tie to any chip, workload or benchmark. Any Studio result would not be numerically comparable to the 46-62 C labels.

The scenario is steady-state 2D and has no 3D stacking, interposer, microchannel or TSV modeling, so those survey topics do not apply. HotSpot's transient RK4 solver and its 3D extensions (HS3D) are not used for Fig. 6.
No controller, optimizer or reliability model is part of the Fig. 6 scenario. The survey explicitly excludes thermal-management policies from its scope (p. 10).

assessment.summary: 2D screening label: illustrative_2d_only (steady 2D is relevant, but only as a schematic). Studio did NOT run: simulation status is skipped because the input gate failed (a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object; floorplan and power_w are empty). The input gate and scientific gate both failed, simulation_allowed is false, and comparison_valid is false. The scenario is Fig. 6 (p. 16) of the survey, a HotSpot modeling-flow schematic with seven power labels (0.2, 0.2, 1, 3, 2, 2, 1 W) and seven temperature labels (46, 46.1, 51, 62, 57, 55, 49 C). It names no blocks, gives no coordinates or dimensions, and does not map powers to blocks. The experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, so there is no transient trace. It is not a bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and no pinned Ascend910/ATPlace assets, source commit, or generated-placement input.flp/input.ptrace exist. The packet has no assets and the paper links no repositories (checked_no_links). The 62 C label is a figure-label maximum with unspecified location, so it cannot be compared numerically to any Studio output. No result exists, and nothing here supports a claim of replication or exact agreement. Only qualitative remarks are defensible: HotSpot-style steady RC models give higher temperatures where per-block power is higher (3 W pairs with the 62 C maximum label, though that pairing is itself unmapped), and temperature depends on package and cooling assumptions that the paper does not specify for this example. The final verdict is no simulation and no valid comparison.
